--- src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__clients.sql ---
-- Clients: the first domain table. Name + email per client.
-- GENERATED BY DEFAULT (not ALWAYS) so the /__test__ seed path can insert explicit fixture ids.
CREATE TABLE clients (
    id    BIGINT       GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name  VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL
);
--- src/main/resources/db/migration/V2__clients_email_format.sql ---
-- Every client must have a PROPER email address. The column was already NOT NULL (V1); this adds a
-- CHECK constraint as the last line of defence behind the front-end and server validation, mirroring
-- their pattern: one @, non-empty local/domain parts, and a dotted domain.
ALTER TABLE clients
    ADD CONSTRAINT clients_email_format
    CHECK (REGEXP_LIKE(email, '^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$'));
--- src/main/resources/db/migration/V3__projects.sql ---
-- Projects: the second domain table. A project has a name and belongs to a client (client_id FK).
-- GENERATED BY DEFAULT (not ALWAYS) so the /__test__ seed path can insert explicit fixture ids.
CREATE TABLE projects (
    id        BIGINT       GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    name      VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    client_id BIGINT       NOT NULL REFERENCES clients(id)
);
--- src/main/resources/db/migration/V4__invoices.sql ---
-- Invoices: the third domain table. An invoice has a monetary amount and belongs to a project
-- (project_id FK). GENERATED BY DEFAULT (not ALWAYS) so the /__test__ seed path can insert
-- explicit fixture ids.
CREATE TABLE invoices (
    id         BIGINT        GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id BIGINT        NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id),
    amount     DECIMAL(12,2) NOT NULL
);
--- src/main/resources/db/migration/V5__invoice_status.sql ---
-- Invoices gain a payment status so an invoice can be marked paid. Additive column with a NOT NULL
-- default of 'UNPAID' so every existing row (and any insert that omits it) starts unpaid; the app
-- flips it to 'PAID' when the invoice is paid.
ALTER TABLE invoices ADD COLUMN status VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNPAID';
--- src/main/resources/db/migration/V6__invoice_dates.sql ---
-- Invoices gain two dates: when the invoice was issued (went out) and when it is due. Additive
-- columns stored as ISO date strings (YYYY-MM-DD) so the value the app surfaces is exactly what was
-- stored — the front-end shows the literal date. Nullable so existing rows are unaffected; the
-- /__test__ seed supplies both for a fixture invoice.
ALTER TABLE invoices ADD COLUMN issued_date VARCHAR(10);
ALTER TABLE invoices ADD COLUMN due_date    VARCHAR(10);

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The agent's test loop (DESIGN.md §15): build, start the whole app, run ONLY the specs currently
# present in e2e/specs (the agent sees only its own checkpoint's spec — blind), then stop.
# PINNED — do not edit. Contract: BASE_CHECKLIST.md §C, §D.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )

## Summary

The change lets a project's invoices be sorted by due date. Since the database (`due_date` column, Flyway V6) and server (`InvoicesGet` returning `dueDate`) already store and surface the due date, this was an additive front-end change following the app's slot/URL-key conventions:

- **`slots/defs/invoicesToolbar.ts`** (new) — declares an `invoices.toolbar` region above a project's invoices list, with `{ projectId }` context.
- **`features/invoices/sort.slot.tsx`** (new) — a self-contained "Sort by due date" control (`data-testid="invoice-sort-due"`) that fills the toolbar and owns the `invoiceSort` URL search-param key.
- **`features/invoices/queries.ts`** — exported the shared `INVOICE_SORT_PARAM` key.
- **`features/invoices/InvoicesTable.tsx`** — renders `<InvoicesToolbar.Slot>` and reads the same `invoiceSort` key to order its rows; due dates are ISO strings so a string compare is chronological (ascending).

No component passes callbacks or imports another feature — the sort control and the list coordinate purely through the shared URL key (CLAUDE.md rules 3–4). No DB migration or server change was needed since the due-date data already flows through.
